sections: JMR EARLY CAREER SCHOLARS IN MATERIALS SCIENCE ANNUAL ISSUE
Atomic layer deposition of vanadium oxide thin /uniFB01 lms from tetrakis(dimethylamino)vanadium precursor
A. ALD of vanadium oxide films
B. Characterizations of precursor and VO x films

figures.caption: FIG. 1. TG curves of V(dma)4 performed under open-cup and closecup conditions.
FIG. 2. Growth rate of VO x /uniFB01 lms as a function of the deposition temperature. Water vapor or ozone was used as the oxygen source.

FIG. 3. Representative XPS results for a 15 nm VO x /uniFB01 lm deposited at 120 °C with H2O as the coreactant. (a) Survey and high-resolution scans for (b) V 2 p , (c) O 1 s , (d) C 1 s , and (e) N 1 s , respectively.

FIG. 4. Representative AFM images for ALD VO x /uniFB01 lms deposited (a) with H2O at 120 °C and (b) with O3 at 80 °C, respectively. The /uniFB01 lm thicknesses were both ; 10 nm, and the corresponding rms roughness values were (a) 0.32 nm and (b) 0.96 nm, respectively.

FIG. 5. XRD spectra of an ALD VO x /uniFB01 lm before and after thermal annealing at 800 °C under N2 ambient for 2 h. The as-deposited /uniFB01 lm (i.e., before annealing) did not show any XRD peaks (the broad feature at 20° -25° was from the fused silica substrate); whereas the annealed /uniFB01 lm showed pronounced XRD peaks which well matched with the pattern of monoclinic VO2 (PDF#44 -0252). The ALD VO x /uniFB01 lm was originally deposited at 50 °C with H2O, and the thickness was ; 60 nm.
FIG. 6. SEM top-view images comparatively showing the accompanying morphological change of the VO x /uniFB01 lm (a) before and (b) after the annealing process as described in Fig. 5.

FIG. 7. In situ HTXRD for an ALD VO x /uniFB01 lm heated from room temperature to 800 °C, with the XRD spectra taken in steps of 50 °C from 200 °C. The XRD spectra started to show pronounced crystalline VO2 peaks at 600 °C.

FIG. 8. In situ QCM measurements for ALD VO x at 50 °C. (a) Mass gain versus time for 50 ALD cycles. (b) Enlarged view for three consecutive ALD cycles. (c) Per cycle mass gain ( m 0) and m 1 / m 0 ratio extracted for each individual ALD cycle.
